To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human growth hormone (hGH) and salmon growth hormone (sGH) both acutely enhance the potential for extrathyroidal 3,5.3-triiodothyronine production in rainbow trout by increasing the level of functional hepatic 5-deiodinase activity without affecting the plasma thyroxine concentration.
sGH, like human GH, acutes enhances extra-thyroid conversion of T4 to T 3 in trout by increasing hepatic 5 '- D activity, but does not affect the plasma T4 or T3 level.

human and salmon growth hormones acutely enhance the potential for extrathyroidal triiodothyronine production in rainbow trout by increasing the activity of hepatic 3,5-3'-triiodothyonine 5'-monodeiodinase without changing the plasma thyroxine concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of salmon pituitary extracts (SP) on the thyroid and the thyroid-dependent processes of growth, osmoregulation and energy metabolism.
the role of thyroid hormones in the regulation of growth and metabolism of rainbow trout.
the role of thyroid hormones (TH) in the regulation of growth and development in fish, and with the role of growth hormone (GH) in stimulating the TH system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GH, whether of salmon, human, bovine, or ovine origin, stimulates the 5'-D activity and the T3 production rate, without altering plasma T4 levels.
the GHs of all species tested to date (human, salmon and trout) stimulate 5'-D activity in the trout liver, but not 5'-D Km. 4.

the effects of GH in the fish, as in other vertebrates, appear to be due to a combination of direct effects on tissue 5'-deioidinase, and indirect effects on the thyroid gland, resulting in increased circulating T4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GH of all vertebrates tested to date, except the GH of the chicken, increases the hepatic 3,5'-5'-D activity and thus the capacity for T4 to be converted to T3.
GH from all species tested so far (human, bovine, ovine and sGH) increases hepatic 5' deiodination in rainbow trout.
GHs from salmon and human stimulate hepatic 5'D activity in trout and thereby increase the potential for T3 production, but without changing plasma T4 levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sGH, like human GH, can acutely stimulate the hepatic T4-to-T3 conversion rate in rainbow trout.
sGH, like hGH, is an acute regulator of the extra-thyroid T3 production pathway.
GH is not a thyroid hormone.
